memories.lesson: Before accepting an extra feature, ask for a separately priced change proposal
Before accepting another revision, check how many agreed revision rounds have been used and ask for clarification if that history is unclear.
When a client asks for another page, clarify whether it is a new deliverable or a replacement for an agreed page before committing.
Before starting work that depends on client content, ask who will supply the final copy and images and when they will be ready.
For a new third-party integration, clarify the service, required access and any recurring charges before committing to implementation.
When a request brings the deadline forward, ask what should be prioritised and whether the scope needs to change before promising the new date.
When feedback from several client stakeholders conflicts, ask the client to consolidate it into one approved direction before making changes.
Before replacing an approved design direction, clarify which earlier decisions are being reopened and what rework is being requested.
When a request includes ongoing support, clarify the support period and responsibilities instead of assuming maintenance is included
In suggested client replies, use one concise paragraph, avoid emoji, and end with one concrete next step without inventing a price or promising approval.
